questions.question: Define census and explain two reasons why accurate population data is important.
questions.expected_answer: A census is an official count of every person in a country at a particular time, collecting information such as age, sex, education, employment and housing; in South Africa it is run by Stats SA (2022: about 62 million). Data is needed to plan schools, clinics, housing, water, electricity and roads; to divide government money between provinces and municipalities; to draw voting boundaries; and for businesses to plan.

questions.question: A district has 80 000 people, 2 000 births and 640 deaths in a year. Calculate the birth rate, death rate, natural increase and growth rate as a percentage.
questions.expected_answer: Birth rate = 2 000 / 80 000 x 1 000 = 25 per thousand. Death rate = 640 / 80 000 x 1 000 = 8 per thousand. Natural increase = 25 - 8 = 17 per thousand = 1.7 percent per year.

questions.question: Explain why a high birth rate does not always mean rapid population growth, and give two needs of a rapidly growing population.
questions.expected_answer: Growth depends on the difference between births and deaths (and migration); if the death rate is also high, natural increase is small, as for most of history. A rapidly growing population is young and needs many schools, teachers, clinics, food, housing, and later jobs.
